entry.title: Regular Truchet tilings
entry.content: Photos and discussion of a 30×40 Truchet canvas print built from Truchet tiles on the truncated trihexagonal tiling, with notes on the 10 PRINT inspiration, Catalan connections for 2n-gons, and links to random-tiling bots and further reading.

entry.title: Stacking LEGO bricks
entry.content: Counting LEGO brick towers: rules and generating-function proofs (including the 3^{n-1} formula for 1×2 bricks), symmetry and OEIS sequences, and notes on stability and overhang problems.

entry.title: Parity bitmaps from the OEIS
entry.content: A Python tool that turns two-dimensional OEIS sequences into one-bit-per-pixel parity bitmaps — featuring a fractal from A279212, example images, downloadable code, and links to further exploration.

entry.title: Polytopes with lattice coordinates
entry.content: Exploring polytopes with lattice coordinates — counting polygons and polyhedra on square, triangular and higher-dimensional grids, surprising lattice examples and embeddings, OEIS sequence cataloging, and an applet illustrating the binomial formula for equilateral triangles.

entry.title: A π-estimating Twitter bot (1 of 3)
entry.content: Part 1 of a three-part guide to @BotfonsNeedles: simulating Buffon's needle in Python to estimate π and generating images in Python for a Twitter bot.

entry.title: A π-estimating Twitter bot (2 of 3)
entry.content: Part 2 of a three-part guide to @BotfonsNeedles: using the Twitter API (tweepy) to post images, read and write tweets, and maintain a running Monte Carlo estimate of π.

entry.title: A π-estimating Twitter bot (3 of 3)
entry.content: Part 2 of a three-part guide to @BotfonsNeedles. Step-by-step guide to containerizing and deploying a π‑estimating Twitter bot, including build a Docker image, create an AWS Lambda container function, and scheduling it.

entry.title: Richard Guy's partition sequence
entry.content: Interpreting Richard Guy’s 1971 letter to Neil Sloane and investigating his partition sequence A279197: corrected definition, Haskell code, and extended OEIS terms counting inseparable, self-conjugate 3-term arithmetic partitions of {1..3n}.

entry.title: My favorite sequences: A261865
entry.content: Exploration of OEIS A261865 — the least integer k whose square root has a multiple in (n,n+1); includes examples, plots, a conjectured density formula for values, and record-finding computations.

entry.title: My favorite sequences: A289523
entry.content: An exploration of OEIS sequence A289523: greedily placing circles of area kπ so they don't overlap, with plots, spiral variants, and questions about linear bounds and packing density.

entry.title: My favorite sequences: "Not Equal" Grid
entry.content: Exploring OEIS sequence A278299 — the minimal polyomino sizes that allow an n-coloring with every pair of colors adjacent; origin, bounds, computations, and a playable solver.

entry.title: My favorite sequences: A263135
entry.content: Explores OEIS A263135—maximal penny-to-penny contacts for n pennies on hexagonal-grid vertices—spiral packings, comparison with face-penny sequence A047932, and a conjectured difference (A216256) with an open-problem bounty.

entry.title: Zimin words and bifixes
entry.content: Explores Zimin words and bifixes in binary strings—counting words that begin with odd/even palindromes, related OEIS sequences, bijections, and pattern-avoidance results.

entry.title: Pour Le Science and the anti-sum-product problem
entry.content: A Pour La Science mention of my OEIS work and the 'anti' sum–product problem: sequences (A337655, A337946) whose addition and multiplication tables maximize distinct values (and in A337946 never overlap), with related OEIS explorations.

entry.title: Robot walks
entry.content: Exploration of Project Euler Problem 208's 'robot walks'—visual demos, interactive applet and code, Stack Exchange discussions, a Twitter bot that tweets walk patterns, and prints inspired by the paths.

entry.title: XOR triangles
entry.content: Exploring the math behind the @xorTriangles bot: generating XOR number triangles, characterizing rotationally symmetric seeds via linear algebra over Z/2, and connections to OEIS.

entry.title: How to make animated math GIFs: LaTeX + TikZ
entry.content: Step-by-step guide to creating animated math GIFs using LaTeX (TikZ) and ImageMagick — render each frame as a transparent PDF page, then convert to an animated GIF (example: randomized colored circles).

entry.title: Triangle center patterns
entry.content: A hypnotic 4K video and accompanying code exploring a discrete-state random dynamical system: iterating and interpolating triangle centers (from Kimberling's ETC) to create colorful geometric patterns inspired by a tweet.

entry.title: An M.C. Escher-inspired poster
entry.content: An M.C. Escher–inspired 27″×40″ poster based on OEIS A368138 (A368138(2)=154), exploring tile rotations and mirrors in n×n repeating patterns; includes notes on enumeration (Davis 1996 and my paper with Bill Keehn) and op-art-like designs — which would you tile your bathroom with?

entry.title: Some saved tweets
entry.content: A curated archive of saved tweets featuring images of mathematical art, optical illusions, origami and paper models, Truchet designs, teaching resources, and other geometry- and math-related posts.

entry.title: Saved video tweets (1 of 3)
entry.content: Four saved video tweets: a cubic curve through nine points, a rubber-band dodecahedron fold, a rolling oloid (with student project), and a public LEGO build at the Tate Modern.

entry.title: Saved video tweets (2 of 3)
entry.content: A set of saved video tweets: Matt Henderson’s triangle-center fractal that inspired my work, Josh Millard’s clip of Olivier Gomis woodworking, Pierre Thibault’s hypnotic topology loop, and Flávio Costa’s pen-plotter synced to Debussy.

entry.title: Saved video tweets (3 of 3)
entry.content: A curated collection of saved video tweets showcasing Rafael Araujo’s geometric art, Keishiro Ueki’s hinged objects, Amy Goodchild’s Genuary illustrations, and Matt Pritchard’s optical illusion.

entry.title: Cube fractals
entry.content: A Mathematica animation inspired by Robert Fathauer's cube-fractal timelapse and Ayliean's #MathArtMarch, exploring shifting cube fractals and transparent views.

entry.title: Vowel cascades
entry.content: FEND. FIND. FOND. FUND. FAND? Inspired by a Bluesky post, I show how I used Python and word lists to find words that satisfy a given set of vowel combinations.

entry.title: JMM Exhibition of Mathematical Art
entry.content: Recreating a 2021 tweet with JMM catalog photos and reflecting on my mathematical art in the 2024 and 2025 JMM exhibitions—photos, video, Bridges links, and pen-plotter/Mathematica projections.

entry.title: Hinged stellated dodecahedron
entry.content: Photos and stories about stellated dodecahedron model from the 2025 JMM art exhibition, which was inspired by early makerspace projects and built using plywood, 8¢ hinges and laser-cut faces

entry.title: "A beautiful little problem!"
entry.content: A "beautiful little problem" about rational roots of quadratic equations with odd coefficients.

entry.title: LEGO Truchet
entry.content: Inspired by Dave Richeson’s Truchet tilings, I designed and built my own LEGO version using Stud.io, Bricklink parts, and a few hundred euros’ worth of curved tiles.

entry.title: Yan Zhang on power and Conway
entry.content: Reflections on Yan Zhang’s threads about status, power, and recognition in mathematics — the damage of status hierarchies, the value of teaching and mentoring, and why John Conway’s playful work is undervalued.

entry.title: G4G15 gift exchange
entry.content: At G4G15 I created 200 hand-cut, pen-plotted 'parity triangle' cards generated from OEIS sequences—made with a Cricut, AxiDraw, and a Python script; includes photos, videos, and info on how to request one.

entry.title: Hexagons in triangles
entry.content: Animations, images, and Mathematica code for inscribing and superimposing hexagonal arrays inside an equilateral triangle, inspired by triangular numbers and a G4G gift-exchange project.

entry.title: Fibonachos
entry.content: Story of 'Fibonachos' — a 2017 reddit puzzle about taking Fibonacci-numbered nachos, my OEIS submissions (A280521, A280523, A382814), Neil Sloane featuring the sequences, and a conjecture about who ends up with the most nachos.

entry.title: Torus tilings
entry.content: Photos and code exploring tiles with reflectional and rotational symmetries, plus programmatic n×m grid and torus tilings using Mathematica and Python.

entry.title: Straightedge and compass (1 of 2)
entry.content: Enumerating distinct straightedge-and-compass constructions with n lines and circles (OEIS A383082–A383087), illustrated with images and a video and computed using Haskell.

entry.title: Straightedge and compass (2 of 2)
entry.content: Images and visualizations of points, lines, and circles obtainable with straightedge-and-compass constructions up to five steps — including 5,743 ruler+compass points, 1,704 compass-only points, 1,337 circles, 596 lines, and 480 compass-only circles, starting from (0,0) and (1,0).

entry.title: Nerd sniped by Richard Stanley
entry.content: An open problem about polyomino tilings, that suggests the possibility of a surprisingly fast-growing function

entry.title: Pentagonal icositetrahedron puzzle
entry.content: A puzzle on the faces of the pentagonal icositetrahedron with 3D models, STL files, photos, and video illustrations

entry.title: RSS for the OEIS
entry.content: An RSS feed based on searches on the On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences

entry.title: Plot party postcard exchange
entry.content: Pen‑plotted polyhedral postcards from a #plot-party — 15 perspectives of nested icosahedron/dodecahedron/icosidodecahedron, with plot timelapses and the postcards I received.

entry.title: Squaring the shelf
entry.content: A shelf design inspired by the 'squaring the square' puzzle, with prototype photos, an interactive 3D model, and downloadable SVG/STL files for laser-cutting or 3D printing.

entry.title: Human rhombic dodecahedron
entry.content: Based on a delightful video of people forming a 'human rhombic dodecahedron,' I look for other examples of human polyhedra with some help from an LAPL librarian.

entry.title: Potato printing plot party postcards
entry.content: A postcard designed for the 2025 plotter postcard exchange #ptpx based on 'Potato Printing,' a game that M.C. Escher played with his kids.

entry.title: G4G16 Gift Exchange
entry.content: The gift I made for Gathering 4 Gardner in 2026, together with files so you can make more at home.

entry.title: Students' favorite Abstract Algebra problems (Fall 2024)
entry.content: A collection of students' favorite problems from my fall 2022 Introduction to Abstract Algebra I class.
